title: Send an e-mail hours later, without ever storing the address
summary: A handoff token lives five minutes, so it cannot be saved for an escalation that happens tonight. The notifier consumes it now, stores only a pseudonym, and fetches the address just in time - which is also why one unsubscribe click stops the mail with no list to scrub.

steps.label: A ticket is opened
steps.note: The customer exists in the CRM with an address and a name.

steps.label: Hand off, authorizing the e-mail and nothing else
steps.note: share_attributes is the issuer saying WHICH fields may appear in the other system. A token cannot be stockpiled - it dies in five minutes - so the notifier must consume it now, at handoff time, not at send time.

steps.label: The notifier consumes it and gets its OWN pseudonym
steps.note: This is the whole trick. The notifier now holds a stable handle for this customer that is unrelated to the CRM's - a leak of the notifier database joins with nothing.

assert.message: the notifier must hold a different pseudonym than the CRM

steps.label: Hours later: fetch the address just in time
steps.note: The notifier stored a ticket id and a pseudonym - no address, no name. When the escalation fires it asks for the e-mail, purpose stated, and the read is consent-checked and on the audit chain.

steps.label: What the issuer did not share is simply not there
steps.note: The name was never authorized, so it never crossed. Not hidden by a filter in the notifier - absent from the notifier's scope entirely.

steps.label: The customer clicks unsubscribe
steps.note: One decision, recorded next to the data it governs.

steps.label: The next escalation cannot get an address
steps.note: No code change in the notifier, no suppression list to maintain, no risk that one forgotten batch job still has a copy: the address is simply no longer obtainable for this purpose.
